audit.title: Cross-Chain Token Standard (SVM)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. The first substantive prose is a token-registration NOTE, not an answer; the description — "provides detailed guidance for integrating tokens…on SVM-based blockchains like Solana" — describes the section rather than defining the concept. A lead sentence stating what CCT on SVM *is* would stand alone.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Adequate for a hub. Measured facts confirm 1 section, 7 bullets, 0 level skips; the annotated link list is scannable, but a single H1 with no H2 grouping limits chunk richness.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Thin — 3 numerals, 0 with units, no version strings (per measured facts). No supported-network specifics, program counts, or standard version. Expected for an index, but a few anchor facts would help retrieval.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 8 internal links (appropriate for a hub) plus one contact form; 0 links to primary sources such as the SPL token or Solana program specs. Acceptable for navigation, not for authority.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Neither "Cross-Chain Token Standard" nor "SVM" is defined in a liftable one-to-two-sentence form near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts show 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent from head. A body "Last Updated: 2025-05-19" exists but is not machine-exposed. `<head>` could not be verified — pass raw head for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable — a hub page needs no snippets; scored neutral, no action needed.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers subtopic navigation but no "how do I…", "what is…", or error/symptom phrasing. It captures browsing intent, not question intent.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Terminology (CCIP, CCT, SVM, SPL) is used consistently; prose is unambiguous.

audit.summary: This is a section-index (hub) page routing developers to the seven SVM-specific Cross-Chain Token subpages. Its strength is clean, consistent navigation with a coherent link list; its biggest weakness is the absence of a self-contained, liftable definition of "Cross-Chain Token Standard on SVM" — the page opens with a process NOTE and a single vague sentence, so an engine has nothing quotable to synthesize. As a hub it is functional, but it currently competes poorly for retrieval on any conceptual or "what is" query and carries no structured metadata to establish trust.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical answer-first definition lead
recommendations.where: First line under the H1, before the NOTE block.
recommendations.issue: "This section provides detailed guidance for integrating tokens…" — describes the section, defines nothing.
recommendations.change: Open with a self-contained sentence, e.g. "The Chainlink CCIP Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard on SVM lets SPL token developers enable their tokens for cross-chain transfer across Solana and other SVM-based chains using token pool programs." Then keep the NOTE below it.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition; defends against parametric priors that would otherwise generalize from EVM CCT docs.

recommendations.title: Add structured metadata (JSON-LD + canonical + dates)
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no machine-readable dateModified (measured facts).
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `inLanguage`, and a canonical URL matching the served page.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and canonical signals raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and disambiguate this SVM page from its EVM counterpart.

recommendations.title: Group links under symptom/intent-phrased subheadings
recommendations.issue: Flat list keyed to page titles, not user questions.
recommendations.change: Add short H2/H3 framing such as "How do I decide my integration path?" (→ Integration Guide) and "What are the SPL token requirements?" (→ Tokens), keeping the existing links as answers.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by task/symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that title-cased prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add a few concrete SVM specifics
recommendations.issue: 3 numerals, 0 units, no networks named beyond "like Solana."
recommendations.change: Name the supported SVM networks explicitly and the token pool program types (e.g. BurnMint, LockRelease) with counts where stable.
recommendations.why: Quantitative and named-entity specifics are among the highest-lift retrieval signals.

recommendations.title: Add one primary-source reference
recommendations.change: Inline-link "SPL tokens" to the Solana SPL token documentation and "SVM" to a canonical Solana VM reference.
recommendations.why: Authoritative outbound links raise citation credibility and aid entity resolution.

antiPatterns: Lead content is a process/administrative NOTE ahead of any conceptual answer — pushes the quotable substance down.
Undated in machine-readable form: "Last Updated: 2025-05-19" is body text only, invisible to parsers.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no broken cross-references — clean on those axes.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good site-level signal; ensure this SVM hub and its 7 children are listed there.
Canonical/JSON-LD emission is likely a site-template concern; fix once at the docs framework level rather than per page.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata presence can be verified rather than inferred as absent.
